turns.responseText:
ABL1 Kinase Inhibitor Pharmacophore Screening — Builds a consensus pharmacophore model from 4 known ABL1 inhibitors and screens a 4-compound library against it in a single run.

Input: reference_smiles = 4 ABL1 inhibitors (Imatinib, Dasatinib, Bosutinib, Asciminib); library_smiles = 4 screening compounds (Gleevec-analog-1, Ponatinib, Terfenadine, Acetaminophen); min_features = 3
Key steps:

RDKit MolChemInformatics → extracts 3D pharmacophoric features (H-bond donors/acceptors, hydrophobic centers, aromatic rings, positive ionizable) from all 4 reference SMILES and builds a consensus pharmacophore model
Pharmacophore Filtering Engine → screens each library compound against the consensus model, requiring ≥ 3 feature matches; scores and ranks hits by feature overlap and geometric fit


Expected output: pharmacophore_hits.csv (ranked library compounds with match scores and matched feature types) + pharmacophore_model.json (consensus feature definitions) + screening_summary.html (visual report with hit/miss classification per compound)


✅ All 4 reference SMILES and all 4 library SMILES have been parsed and passed directly into the pharmacophore_filtering workflow. Click Run to execute — no additional data entry needed. Results will flag likely ABL1-active scaffolds (e.g., Ponatinib, Gleevec-analog-1) while filtering out off-target or insufficiently complex compounds (e.g., Acetaminophen).

turns.responseText:
BCR-ABL1 Campaign Safety-Potency Ranking — Ingests dual-assay IC50 data for 15 compounds and produces a composite rank ordered by kinase potency and cardiac safety.

Input: 30-row assay CSV (15 compounds × 2 assay types: IC50_BCR_ABL1 in nM + hERG_IC50 in µM, dated 2026-03-15)
Key steps:

CSV parser → normalizes units, pivots to wide format (one row per compound)
Composite scorer → log-transforms IC50 values, applies weighted rank (BCR-ABL1 potency 60% / hERG safety 40%), flags hERG IC50 < 1 µM as cardiac risk
Report generator → outputs ranked compound table + HTML summary with traffic-light safety annotations


Expected output: ranked_compounds.csv (rank, composite score, BCR-ABL1 IC50, hERG IC50, cardiac-risk flag) + HTML report with interactive ranking table + JSON summary of scoring metadata

Decision gate: hERG IC50 < 1 µM → automatic RED flag (cardiac liability; CPD009 at 0.08 µM and CPD010 at 0.05 µM expected to rank last); BCR-ABL1 IC50 < 1 nM + hERG IC50 > 10 µM → GREEN / Priority tier (CPD004–CPD006 expected #1–2 candidates).

turns.responseText:
CRO Submission Export — WuXi AppTec (BCR-ABL1 Campaign) — Validates cardiac safety and formats all 5 ranked compounds into a WuXi-ready CSV export package.

Input: 5 compounds with SMILES — Asciminib (#1), Bosutinib (#2), Imatinib (#3), Gleevec-analog-2 (#4), Gleevec-analog-1 (#5) — plus IC50 (nM), hERG IC50 (μM), and composite score from campaign ranking
Key steps:

hERG cardiac safety gate → flags any compound with hERG IC50 ≤ 1 μM as a blocker; all 5 must pass before export proceeds
RDKit property calculation → computes MW and LogP from each SMILES, appends to compound record
WuXi AppTec CSV formatter → maps compound_id / SMILES / IC50 / hERG IC50 / composite score / MW / LogP to WuXi column schema → wuxiapptec_submission.csv + metadata JSON


Expected output: wuxiapptec_submission.csv (WuXi-formatted, all 5 compounds if cardiac-safe) + submission_metadata.json (batch ID, safety gate pass/fail per compound, timestamp)

Decision gate: hERG IC50 > 1 μM required for all compounds — any compound failing this threshold is automatically excluded from the export CSV and flagged in the metadata report before CRO handoff.
